text:
Priya: Heads up 10:20 UTC10:42 UTC we saw privilege errors in the onprem keystore agent and suspicious audit gaps. Flagging as P2 for now.
Alex: Which cluster/region? Any customer impact?
Priya: onprem-cluster-3 (eu-nl colo). No external customer data exfiltrated but some decrypt audit events missing for ~20m.
Tessa: I pulled node syslogs, seeing repeated kernel drops around 10:21: `DROP IN=eth0 OUT= MAC=... PROTO=TCP SPT=8443 DPT=44512`. Looks like egress to kms-proxy failing on certain nodes.
Raj: Was there any RBAC or CRB change during the maintenance window?
Priya: We merged a CRB tightening for `audit-uploader` at 10:18 (PR #1209) that changed subjects from `system:serviceaccount:infra:legacy-sa` to `system:serviceaccount:infra:audit-writer-sa`. The mapping was supposed to be a one-to-one rename, but the infra CI job also generated a short-lived token for the old SA that might still be active.
Alex: infra-bot, show deploy and iam events 10:15-10:30 UTC for cluster-3.
infra-bot: deploy-event: `priv-keystore-rollout-2026-03-22` at 10:19 UTC. iam-event: `kubectl create clusterrolebinding audit-uploader` (diff attached).
Priya: Forensics: can we confirm which principal made the GenerateDataKey and PutObject calls during window?
forensics-bot: CloudTrail-like logs (local audit) show GenerateDataKey called by principal `system:serviceaccount:infra:legacy-sa` until 10:20:30, then AccessDenied. PutObject attempts continued but failed with 403 on 10:21:xx.
Tessa: So the old SA's token was revoked or its mapping dropped mid-rolling restart resulting in intermittent failures. Also noticed a concurrent iptables CNI bump that enforces egress from pods by label at 10:22. Two changes at same time 1erf.
Raj: Root cause hypothesis: race between CRB remap + CNI egress tighten causing some pods to lose KMS proxy access and inability to assume uploader role -> audit writes buffered locally -> missing audit events.
Alex: Mitigation plan (short): 1) Temporarily widen egress policy to allow pod CIDR range 172.20.0.0/16 to kms-proxy port 8443, 2) re-create legacy SA mapping for continuity while we rotate tokens, 3) requeue buffered audit files to s3, 4) snapshot nodes for forensics.
Priya: I'll coordinate step 2 and token rotation (Priya owns). Tessa take step 1. Raj run reingest. Alex will file incident and owner the postmortem.
Tessa: Applying netpol rollback now: `kubectl apply -f netpol/allow-17220-temp.yaml -n infra`
Tessa: rollback applied at 10:28 UTC.
Raj: Restarting audit-writer pods to force re-registration to uploader role.
Raj: reingest started; processing buffered files from `/var/log/keystore-buffer/` . Chunked reupload script output:
```
reingest: found 432 files, starting batch upload
reingest: uploaded 360 files (ok), 72 pending
```
Raj: Will follow up when full reingest done.
Priya: Forensic note: capture kube-apiserver audit logs and host journal from impacted nodes (done, attached to ticket). Also rotate any short-lived tokens tied to legacy-sa.
forensics-bot: Snapshot created: nodes srv-3a,srv-3b,srv-3c at 10:31 UTC.
Alex: Follow-ups (post incident): - Add CI gate preventing simultaneous CRB changes + netpol rollouts in same window - Add automated egress test from both primary and secondary CIDRs - Add monotonic handoff: ensure SA remap done before token invalidation and rolling restarts.
Priya: Filing change to our runbook: verify GenerateDataKey success to CMEK/CloudTrail before closing any remap.
Raj: Reingest completed at 10:40 UTC; recovered 99.6% of buffered events. Missing ~2 files from srv-3c where local disk rotated before capture. Noted in incident ticket.
Tessa: Once we bake the fix, I'll reapply strict netpol with explicit cidr mappings and add e2e test.
Alex: Incident ticket PRIV-KEYSTORE-1750022468 created. Marking this thread as primary log. Thanks all.
Priya: Closing note: low blast radius but good catch; we'll push the guardrails. Keep any anomalies in ticket.
